# Intake brief — Keep focus on the Herdr selection list when a shortcut command creates a pane

## Problem statement

Executing a shortcut command from the Herdr work item selection list (worklist pane) creates a new pane — a pi agent pane (for `/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:` commands) or a command-output pane (for `!!`/`!` and plain shell commands). The new pane then takes focus, moving the user away from the selection list mid-workflow. The selection list pane should keep focus so the user can continue browsing and dispatching.

## Users

Herdr Worklog plugin users who drive their work-item workflow from the keyboard-navigable selection list.

- As a user browsing the selection list, I want to run `/skill:implement <id>` and keep my place in the list, so I can queue up more work without re-navigating.
- As a user approving/rejecting items (`!!wl ...` audit commands), I want the command to run in a pane I can inspect later without yanking focus away from the list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Executing an agent command from the selection list (e.g. `/skill:implement <id>`, `/intake <id>`, `/prompt:...`) opens the pi agent pane WITHOUT moving focus; the selection list keeps focus. Verified by a unit test asserting the dispatch passes `--no-focus` to `send-to-pi.sh`.
- [ ] AC2 — Executing a `!!`/`!`-prefixed command from the selection list (e.g. audit approve/reject, priority updates) opens the command-output pane WITHOUT moving focus. Verified by a unit test asserting `run-in-pane.sh` is dispatched with the no-focus option.
- [ ] AC3 — Executing a plain (unprefixed) shell command from the selection list likewise opens the command-output pane WITHOUT moving focus.
- [ ] AC4 — `run-in-pane.sh` gains a `--no-focus` option (parsed before the command, alongside `--cwd`); when set, the final pane zoom is skipped. Without the flag, current focus behavior is unchanged (backward compatible). Covered by a bash test in `scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh`.
- [ ] AC5 — Out-of-scope behavior unchanged: downtime-worker dispatch panes remain `--no-focus`; the `open-pi-agent` herdr action and `open.sh`/`toggle.sh` keep their current focus behavior; the pane still opens and the command still runs (only focus changes).
- [ ] AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (command routing / design decisions), and script usage docs.
- [ ] AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Shared launchers `shared/send-to-pi.sh` and `shared/open-pi-agent.sh` are reusable by other plugins/consumer projects (see `shared/README.md`) — their defaults must NOT change; the worklist dispatch passes `--no-focus` explicitly.
- `run-in-pane.sh` must remain backward compatible for existing callers/tests that rely on the current focus behavior.
- Only the focus behavior changes — pane creation, command execution, pane naming, and lifecycle (`--exec` wrapper, stay-open behavior) are untouched.
- The new pane must still open in the resolved project root (`--cwd` arg > `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` > `$PWD`), unchanged.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — the `onCommand` callback routes every selection-list command:
  - `agent` route (`/skill:`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:`): spawns `scripts/send-to-pi.sh` with `buildSendToPiArgs(command, targetCwd, model, paneIdFile)` → `['--cwd', <cwd> [, '--model', <model>] [, '--pane-id-file', <file>], <prompt>]`. No `--no-focus`, so `shared/send-to-pi.sh` (default `focus=true`) zooms the new pane at the end (`pane zoom <np> --on` + `--off`).
  - `pane` route (`!!`/`!`): spawns `scripts/run-in-pane.sh` with `['--cwd', targetCwd, <clean-command>]`.
  - `stdout` route (plain): spawns `scripts/run-in-pane.sh` with `['--cwd', targetCwd, <command>]`.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — splits with `--no-focus`, then unconditionally focuses the new pane at the end:
  ```bash
  "$herdr_bin" pane zoom "$np" --on >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  "$herdr_bin" pane zoom "$np" --off >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  ```
  It has no `--no-focus` option.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — already parses `--no-focus`; the downtime worker already passes it (`buildDowntimePaneArgs` in `src/downtime-worker.ts`).
- Command-send feedback is surfaced via Herdr toast notifications (`notify.ts`), so a no-focus dispatch does not leave the user without feedback.

## Desired change

1. `src/index.ts` — agent route: include `--no-focus` in the `send-to-pi.sh` argument vector (in `buildSendToPiArgs`, which is testable and used only by this dispatch).
2. `scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — add a `--no-focus` flag parsed before the command (alongside `--cwd`); skip the final zoom when set.
3. `src/index.ts` — `pane` and `stdout` routes: pass `--no-focus` to `run-in-pane.sh`.
4. Tests: extend `scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh` (bash) for the `--no-focus` flag; extend `src/index.test.ts` for `buildSendToPiArgs`/dispatch args; confirm `shared/tests/test_scripts.sh` `--no-focus` coverage still applies.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `onCommand` dispatch; add `--no-focus` to agent (`buildSendToPiArgs`) and pane/stdout (`run-in-pane.sh`) spawn args.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — add `--no-focus` option; gate the final zoom on it.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — unit tests for the `--no-focus` argument on both dispatch paths.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh` — bash test that `--no-focus` skips zoom and that omitting it preserves current behavior.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — update command-routing / design-decision docs to state that panes spawned from the selection list open without stealing focus.

## Related work

- WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K (Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime) — established the `--no-focus` pattern for `send-to-pi.sh` (`buildDowntimePaneArgs`); precedent for this change.
- WL-0MSDZ6A6M0014SHB (Resize mode in shared launch scripts) — related shared-launch-script option work.
- WL-0MSAPRMRH002S10O (Add pane-launch option to shared herdr code) — related shared-launch options.
- WL-0MSDZ69TZ00962IO (Shared grid helper grid.py) — grid.py powers the resize mode in these scripts.
- WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ (Subscribe to herdr window events instead of polling active window status) — open; adjacent focus/visibility behavior, not blocking.
- `packages/herdr/shared/README.md` — documents the shared launchers and their `--focus`/`--no-focus` options.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: the no-focus behavior applies to ALL commands dispatched from the selection list (agent, `!!`/`!`, and plain shell) — confirmed with the operator.
- Assumption: `open-pi-agent` (herdr plugin action) and the downtime worker keep their current behavior — confirmed with the operator (scope question; `open-pi-agent` is an unbound action, not part of the selection-list dispatch).
- Risk (low): users may not immediately notice a command pane opened in the background. Mitigation: toast feedback on dispatch (`notify.ts`) and the pane remains visible; the user can focus it manually with herdr pane navigation.
- Risk (low): adding a `--no-focus` option to `run-in-pane.sh` must not break commands whose first token begins with `--` (only `--cwd`/`--no-focus` are treated as options at the head of the argv; everything else is the command).
- Scope-creep guard: no new settings/configurability requested — hard-code no-focus for the selection-list dispatch. If a toggle is wanted later, track as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the no-focus behavior apply to (a) both selection-list command paths only (agent panes + command-output panes), or (b) also the `open-pi-agent` herdr action?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): "when is open-pi-agent used?" — Agent researched usage: it is an unbound herdr plugin action (`herdr-plugin.toml` → `scripts/open-pi-agent.sh`), not referenced by the selection-list TUI (`worklist.ts`/`index.ts`), and has no keybinding in `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` (only `prefix+l` → open-worklist and `prefix+p` → podcast). The underlying `shared/open-pi-agent.sh` is a reusable utility for other plugins/consumer projects. User then confirmed: "proceed" with assumption (a).
  - Final accepted answer: scope = selection-list dispatch paths only (`send-to-pi.sh` agent route + `run-in-pane.sh` pane/stdout routes). `open-pi-agent.sh`, downtime worker, and `open.sh`/`toggle.sh` unchanged. Source: interactive reply, repo/config inspection.
- Q: "My default assumption is (a) — the selection-list command dispatch only." — Answer (user): "proceed". Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J** – Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM) (completed)
- **WL-0MO5XN3WK005CDS7** – Dialog key propagation bugs (completed)
- **WL-0MSEPOZVF006VOZY** – Command log module implementation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: agent, command, executes, focus, focused (+13 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: agent, command, executes, intent, item (+13 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — matched: agent, command, executes, intent, item (+12 more)

# Detail view ToC overflows pane — first lines scroll off the top of the screen

## Problem statement

In the Herdr plugin's work-item detail view, when an item has a `Related Docs` Table of Contents (ToC) (i.e. ≥1 `.md` Key File), the rendered output exceeds the pane height: the header (id/title) and the first ToC lines scroll off the top of the screen, so the ToC is not entirely visible. The ToC is also rendered twice and the item header is dropped entirely.

## Users

- **Herdr users** viewing a work item's detail view in the plugin pane, who need the item header and the full `Related Docs` ToC visible at the top of the pane while the metadata/description/document body scrolls beneath.

### Example User Stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the item id, title, and the complete Related Docs ToC when I open a work item's detail view, so nothing important is cut off at the top of the screen.
- As a Herdr user, I want the ToC to stay pinned while I scroll the document, so I can always see which documents are linked to the item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When an item has a ToC (≥1 `.md` Key File), the detail view shows the header (id, title, separator) and the **full** ToC at the top of the pane at scroll 0 — no lines cut off. The ToC is rendered **exactly once** (no duplication), and the item header is present.
2. Detail-view output never exceeds the pane: `formatDetailView` returns at most `viewportHeight` lines, and the full renderer (`createListRenderer` detail mode) returns at most `rows - 1` lines — the line-count invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO holds for detail mode with a ToC present.
3. The header + ToC block stays **pinned** at the top while the body (metadata table, description, md viewer) scrolls beneath it; scrolling is limited to the body region (viewport height minus the pinned block height), and `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` clamps against the same reduced body viewport. No dead/blank region at the bottom when fully scrolled.
4. Items **without** `.md` Key Files (no ToC) keep the existing full-scroll behavior unchanged (regression check — no behavior change for the no-ToC path).
5. Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover: line-count invariant for detail mode with ToC (renderer ≤ `rows - 1`; `formatDetailView` ≤ `viewportHeight`), header + ToC fully visible at scroll 0, ToC not duplicated, pinned-ToC scroll regression (existing `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'` test kept green/updated), and no-ToC behavior unchanged.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant README/docs entries describing the detail-view ToC layout (`packages/herdr/README.md`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Preserve the pinned-ToC design from WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I / WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29: the ToC stays visible on all renders; only the body below it scrolls.
- Respect the line-count invariant established in WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO: the renderer must never emit more than `rows - 1` lines, otherwise the terminal scrolls the top of the output off the pane.
- Surgical change: do not alter scrolling behavior for items without a ToC (the pre-existing full-scroll path).
- No new dependencies; reuse the existing `formatDetailToC` / `formatDetailContent` helpers.

## Existing state

- `formatDetailView` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, ~line 1223) builds the detail output as `[...tocLines, ...bodyLines.slice(safeOffset, safeOffset + viewportHeight)]` where `bodyLines = allLines.slice(tocLines.length)`.
- The slicing assumes the ToC occupies the first `tocLines.length` lines of `allLines`, but `formatDetailContent` emits the header first (blank, id, title, separator = 4 lines) and the ToC **after** it. Consequences (verified by reproduction): (a) the header is dropped from the output, (b) the ToC is duplicated (once from `tocLines`, once inside `bodyLines`), (c) total output = `viewportHeight + tocLines.length` lines, which overflows the pane (`viewportHeight = rows - 1` in the renderer). Reproduction: `formatDetailView(item, 80, 0, 20)` with a 2-entry ToC returns 26 lines; the renderer on a 24-row terminal emits 29 lines (max allowed 23).
- Regression introduced in commit `76a52c9f` (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I, "Implementation complete").
- `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` (~line 496) computes `maxScroll` against the full `viewportHeight` instead of the body region, so clamping is also wrong for the pinned layout.
- The existing test `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'` only asserts the ToC appears in the first 8 lines — it never checks the total line count, so it passes despite the overflow.

## Desired change

1. In `formatDetailView`, compute a **pinned block** = header (4 lines: blank, id, title, separator) + `tocLines`; the scrollable **body** = `allLines.slice(pinnedHeight)`; the **body viewport** = `max(1, viewportHeight - pinnedHeight)`; `maxScroll = max(0, bodyLines.length - bodyViewport)`. Render `[...pinned, ...bodyLines.slice(safeOffset, safeOffset + bodyViewport)]` and update the scroll-indicator percentage math to use `bodyViewport`.
2. Keep the no-ToC path (`tocLines.length === 0`) identical to the pre-ToC behavior (whole content scrolls, header included) to avoid scope creep.
3. Update `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` to clamp against the reduced body viewport (subtract the pinned height) so `j`/`G` behave consistently with the renderer.
4. Optionally introduce a named constant (e.g. `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES = 4`) documenting the fixed header shape so the slicing is self-explanatory.
5. Add/extend unit tests per AC5; update `packages/herdr/README.md` if it describes the detail-view layout.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatDetailView` pinned header+ToC slicing and body-viewport math; `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` clamp; optional header-lines constant.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — line-count invariant tests for detail mode with ToC, header/ToC visibility at scroll 0, no-duplication check, no-ToC regression, updated pinned-ToC test.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the pinned header + ToC detail-view layout if it describes the ToC behavior.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Header-shape fragility:** the fix relies on the header being exactly 4 lines (blank, id, title, separator). Mitigate by introducing a named `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES` constant next to `formatDetailContent` and by an AC1 test asserting the header is visible at scroll 0.
- **No-ToC regression:** altering `formatDetailView` slicing could accidentally change the full-scroll path for items without `.md` Key Files. Mitigate with AC4 regression test asserting the no-ToC path is unchanged.
- **Viewport-height mismatch:** the state class uses `rows - 4` while the renderer uses `rows - 1`; today the renderer's clamp absorbs the difference. The fix must subtract the pinned height consistently in both `formatDetailView` and `detailScrollDown` so `j`/`G` and the on-screen clamp agree.
- **Scope creep:** pinning the header for ALL items (even without a ToC) is deliberately out of scope — it is a UX change beyond the reported bug. Recorded as an assumption; can be tracked as a separate work item if desired.
- **Assumption:** the fix pins header + ToC together (the header sits above the ToC in the content stream, so pinning the ToC keeps the header visible) and scrolls only the body (metadata/description/md viewer) beneath — faithful to the pinned-ToC design intent (WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 AC3) and the user's expectation that the first lines be visible.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I` (completed) — "Herdr: detail-view ToC for Related Docs (arrow/j/k navigate, Enter renders)" — the pinned-ToC implementation that introduced this regression (commit `76a52c9f`).
- `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` (completed) — "Herdr plugin: add Related Docs row to metadata section listing .md Key Files (openable in the markdown viewer)" — defines the pinned-ToC design intent.
- `WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO` (completed) — "Herdr: pane line-count invariant (rows - 1)" — the invariant the detail view now violates.
- `WL-0MS31WX9C008FIQR` (completed) — "Full scrollable detail view" — original detail-view scrolling design (whole content scrolls).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required for this intake.

- The seed report ("The table of contents on the detail view of work items is not entirely visible — the first few lines are off the top of the screen") combined with repository analysis was conclusive: the root cause was located by inspection of `formatDetailView`/`formatDetailContent` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, confirmed by a reproduction test (26 lines emitted for a 20-line viewport; 29 lines for a 24-row terminal vs. the 23-line invariant), and pinned to the regression commit `76a52c9f` (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I) via `git log -S`.
- Assumption (documented, user can override): the fix pins the **header + ToC** block at the top of the detail view (the header is above the ToC in the content stream, so pinning the ToC necessarily keeps the header visible) while the body scrolls beneath — this is the faithful reading of the pinned-ToC design intent in WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 AC3 ("The ToC stays visible on all renders") and the user's expectation that the first lines be visible.
- Assumption (documented, user can override): items **without** `.md` Key Files keep the existing full-scroll behavior unchanged (surgical scope).

---

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKXJPCDI1FLYDB1** – Prompt input box must resize on word wrap (completed)
- **WL-0MRMCO4WX0073W30** – Arbitrary-depth chords in detail view (completed)
- **WL-0MQQW534Q009JSX7** – Remove superfluous ## Stage section from wl create output (completed)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: detail, entirely, first, items, lines (+11 more)

# Auto-revert in_review items to plan_complete when marked not ready to close

## Problem Statement

When a work item in the `in_review` stage (status `completed`) is marked "not ready to close" — via `wl update <id> --audit-text "Ready to close: No"` or `wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no` — nothing happens to the item's lifecycle state. The item remains `completed`/`in_review`, which signals to the heartbeat and release tooling that it is awaiting closure. An item whose audit says it is *not* ready to close should no longer be presented as awaiting closure; its stage should revert to `plan_complete` so it returns to the planning queue for further work.

## Users

- **Producers / reviewers** who audit an `in_review` item, find it lacking, and mark it "not ready to close".
  - *As a producer, I want an in_review item I mark as "not ready to close" to drop out of the ready-to-close queue automatically, so it isn't swept up by heartbeat/release tooling.*
- **Agents / automation** that run audits and write `Ready to close: No` verdicts.
  - *As an agent, I want the lifecycle state to stay consistent automatically when I mark an item not ready, so I don't have to remember to reset status/stage manually.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When `wl update <id> --audit-text "Ready to close: No"` is run on an item with stage `in_review` (status `completed`), the item is automatically reverted to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`.
2. When `wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no` is run on an item with stage `in_review` (status `completed`), the item is automatically reverted to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`.
3. The item's priority is unchanged by the reversion (priority is preserved, not reset).
4. No reversion occurs when the item is not in the `in_review`/`completed` state (e.g., `done` stage, or already `open`/`in-progress`), or when the audit verdict is "Ready to close: Yes" — behavior is otherwise unchanged.
5. The reversion is reported: JSON output includes the reverted item's `from`/`to` status and stage, and human-readable output prints a summary line (e.g. `[WL-XXX reverted from completed/in_review to open/plan_complete]`), following the reporting style of the priority-downgrade cascade.
6. Unit tests cover: reversion via `--audit-text`, reversion via `audit-set`, no-op on `done` items, no-op on non-in_review items, no-op on "Ready to close: Yes", and priority preservation.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The reversion must only fire on the "not ready to close" verdict (`Ready to close: No` / `--ready-to-close no`), not on any other audit text.
- The transition must respect `statusStageCompatibility`: `open` status already permits `plan_complete` stage, so the target state is valid per existing rules.
- The audit write must remain best-effort; if the reversion's `db.update` fails (e.g., file lock), the command should not crash — surface a warning (mirroring the sibling demotion item's best-effort guidance).
- The audit text write path must not be blocked by the existing "skip db.update() when no fields changed" safety guard in `update.ts` — the reversion is an intentional lifecycle consequence of the audit verdict, not an accidental field change.

## Existing State

- `wl update --audit-text` writes to the `audit_results` table via `db.saveAuditResult()` in `src/commands/update.ts` (~line 219–246); a safety guard skips `db.update()` when no work-item fields changed (~line 358).
- `wl audit-set` writes the audit result in `src/commands/audit-result.ts` (~line 154–165) without touching status/stage.
- The API-level audit write path in `src/api.ts` (`normalizeUpdateInputWithAudit`, `writeAuditResult`) also persists audit results without lifecycle changes.
- `statusStageCompatibility` in `config.defaults.yaml`: `open: [idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_progress]` — `open`/`plan_complete` is a valid combination.
- Sibling item WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6 implements the same demotion pattern (`completed`/`in_review` → `open`/`plan_complete`) triggered by adding a child — same target state, different trigger, and shares the reporting convention.

## Desired Change

Implement the reversion as a shared helper (e.g., `revertToPlanComplete(item, db)` or similar) called after an audit write whenever the verdict is not-ready-to-close and the item's stage is `in_review` / status `completed`:

1. **`src/commands/update.ts`** — after a successful `db.saveAuditResult` when the parsed verdict is `Ready to close: No`, check the item state and revert if `in_review`/`completed`.
2. **`src/commands/audit-result.ts`** — in the `audit-set` action, after `db.saveAuditResult` when `--ready-to-close no`, apply the same reversion.
3. **`src/api.ts`** — decide whether the API audit write path (`writeAuditResult` / `normalizeUpdateInputWithAudit`) should also trigger the reversion for consistency; if yes, apply the same helper.
4. **Reporting** — extend JSON output with a `reverted` field (`{ from: { status, stage }, to: { status, stage } }`) and add a human summary line, following the priority-downgrade cascade style.
5. **Tests** — add unit/integration tests covering AC 1–6 (see `tests/cli/audit-results-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/audit.test.ts`, and any update-command test files).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--audit-text` write path; add reversion after not-ready verdict
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` — `wl audit-set` action; add reversion after `--ready-to-close no`
- `src/api.ts` — API-level audit write path; apply reversion for consistency (decision needed)
- `src/audit.ts` — audit parsing helpers (`inspectAuditFirstLine`, `buildAuditEntry`) already produce the ready-to-close verdict
- `src/persistent-store.ts` — `saveAuditResult` / `getAuditResult`; `update` for the reversion write
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` — document the reversion behavior
- `tests/cli/audit-results-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/audit.test.ts` — audit CLI test coverage

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6** ("Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added", ContextHub, open/intake_complete) — implements the same `completed`/`in_review` → `open`/`plan_complete` demotion triggered by adding a child. This item is the mirror trigger (not-ready-to-close audit verdict). Shared helper and reporting convention; the two should not conflict.
- **WL-0MMS4EUMU15LEU7B** ("Audit Write Path (CLI/API)", ContextHub, completed) — established the audit write paths that this change hooks into.
- **WL-0MPZNK0UW009CI6C** ("Implementation: wl audit set subcommand", ContextHub, completed) — the `audit-set` command this change extends.
- **WL-0MRSGMTYU009OZCF** ("Add --audit-file to wl audit-set", ContextHub, completed) — related `audit-set` surface area.
- **WL-0MNFSCMDU0075BMH** ("Audit parser rejects valid 'Ready to close' audits; improve error message", ContextHub, completed) — the first-line audit parsing that determines the verdict.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: extending the reversion to the API path (`src/api.ts`) may surface API consumers that depend on audit writes not changing lifecycle state. Mitigation: if the API path proves risky, restrict reversion to the two CLI commands and record API consistency as a separate follow-up item.
- **Assumption**: "not ready to close" means exactly the audit verdict `Ready to close: No` (or `--ready-to-close no`); no other audit text triggers reversion.
- **Assumption**: reversion target is status `open` / stage `plan_complete` per user answers; priority is preserved (user answer: "the medium is for this item, for the items being reset the priority should remain unchanged").
- **Assumption**: reversion is reported in output (JSON field + human line), mirroring the priority-downgrade cascade and the sibling demotion item's reporting convention.
- **Risk**: the existing safety guard in `update.ts` ("skip db.update() when no fields changed") must be deliberately bypassed only for the intentional reversion — implement carefully to avoid accidental transitions on other audit texts.
- **Risk**: batch `wl update` over multiple ids where some are in_review will revert each qualifying item independently; must not break non-qualifying items in the same batch.

The seed intent says `--priority medium` — should this override the item's current priority? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "No the medium is for this item, for the items being reset the priority should remain unchanged" → `medium` is the priority of THIS work item; reverted items keep their priority.

# Feature Request / Bug: FTS index freshness + silent query-error swallowing

## Problem statement

`wl search` help advertises "Full-text search over work items (title, description, comments, tags)" — and comment indexing is implemented and *works after a manual rebuild* (verified: column-scoped `comments:"Closed with reason"` MATCH returns rows; 1,567/2,462 indexed rows contain comment text; `wl search '"v0.1.11"'` returns comment matches). Two defects make comment search unreliable in practice:

1. **The FTS index is never updated incrementally.** `upsertFtsEntry(item)` (dist/persistent-store.js:963) is defined but has **zero call sites** — it is dead code. `saveWorkItem` / `saveComment` do not touch `worklog_fts`. The index only refreshes via the manual `wl search --rebuild-index` command. Any work item or comment created/edited since the last rebuild is invisible to search — silently stale results (recent items/comments missing, duplicates not detected by triage heuristics).

2. **Malformed FTS5 queries fail silently.** An unquoted punctuated query such as `wl search v0.1.11` produces an FTS5 syntax error (`fts5: syntax error near "."`) that the catch block (persistent-store.js ~1157) swallows, returning `[]` with no warning. Users cannot distinguish "no matches" from "invalid query". Version strings, file paths, and ids (all common search targets in this tool) are exactly the strings that trip this.

## User stories

- As an agent deduplicating test-failure work items, I want recently added comments and items to appear in `wl search` without requiring a manual `--rebuild-index`, so I don't create duplicates.
- As a user searching for `v0.1.11` or a file path, I want either correct matches or an explicit "invalid query" error, not a silent empty result.

## Expected behaviour

- Creating/updating a work item or adding/deleting a comment keeps the FTS index current (call `upsertFtsEntry` from the save paths; call `deleteFtsEntry` from item/comment delete paths).
- FTS5 query syntax errors are surfaced to the user (non-zero exit + clear message), not swallowed; only genuinely zero-match queries return empty results.
- Consider quoting/escaping hygiene: document (and optionally auto-quote) punctuated terms; an option like `--rebuild-index` remains as the backstop for bulk migrations.
- Optional: automatic index rebuild (or per-item reindex) when the index is detected empty/stale (e.g. hash-based staleness already used for embeddings).

## Suggested implementation approach

1. Wire `upsertFtsEntry` into `saveWorkItem` (dist/persistent-store.js:299) and into `saveComment`/comment-delete paths (comments currently don't trigger any FTS update at all).
2. Change `searchFts`'s catch block to rethrow/flag syntax errors (or validate the query with a dry MATCH first) so the command layer can report `error: invalid query syntax` with the offending term.
3. Add unit tests: new item searchable immediately after save; new comment searchable immediately after add; punctuated query error surfaces; delete removes from index.

## Acceptance criteria

1. After `wl create` + `wl comment add`, both the title and the comment text are found by `wl search` WITHOUT running `--rebuild-index`.
2. `wl search v0.1.11` (unquoted punctuated term) exits non-zero with a clear "invalid query — quote phrases" message instead of silently returning 0.
3. Deleting an item/comment removes it from subsequent search results.
4. `wl search --rebuild-index` still works as the manual backstop; full test suite passes.

## Related work

- related-to: SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents) — its analysis assumed comments were not searchable; this request resolves that gap and would enable comment-based remediation queries (e.g. `shipped in v1.0.0` close-reason sweep).
- related-to: WL-0MSLW8GHQ0092PJK — `--fields` projection for list/search; both improve wl CLI efficiency.

# Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching (cheap on operator idle, fast on operator command)

## Problem statement

The llama-proxy runs in two operating modes — **fast** (cloud-backed, 3-slot pool) and **cheap** (2-slot local-first pool). Today mode is switched manually (admin API/UI) or on a fixed time schedule; there is no link between *operator presence* and mode. When an operator is actively working through the herdr plugin, every Pi command should be served by **fast** mode; when the operator leaves (no agent-route Pi commands through the plugin for a configurable window), the proxy should drop to **cheap** mode so the downtime worker's autonomous dispatches consume only the cheap local pool.

## Users

- **Operator running the herdr worklog plugin + llama-proxy** — wants fast responses while actively working and zero-cost cheap mode when away, without touching the mode API by hand.

Example user stories:

- *"As an operator, when I issue an agent command (/skill:*, /intake, /plan, /prompt:) through the herdr plugin, I want the proxy switched to fast mode immediately so my session is served by the cloud-backed pool."*
- *"As an operator, when I have issued no agent-route Pi commands through the plugin for 15 minutes, I want the proxy switched to cheap mode (only when it is idle) so the downtime dispatcher's work runs on the cheap local pool."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Operator-activity tracking:** the plugin records a timestamp on every **agent-route** command (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:` — the routes that spawn a pi agent pane); shell shortcuts (`!!`/`!`) and plain commands do NOT count as operator activity.
- [ ] **Cheap switch on idle:** when no operator agent-route command has been routed for ≥ `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` (default `900000` = 15 min, configurable) **AND** the proxy reports idle (reusing the existing `/llama/local/status` idle evaluation: llama-server running, no active local query, no model switch, no local lease, all required slots free), the worker POSTs `/admin/set-mode {"mode":"cheap"}`. A busy proxy (active local query) **delays** the switch (never kills in-flight work).
- [ ] **Fast switch on command:** when a new operator agent-route command is routed through the plugin, it immediately POSTs `/admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}` (fire-and-forget; a failed switch never blocks or delays the command dispatch — the pane opens regardless, fail-open).
- [ ] **No redundant switching / no hammering:** the worker skips a switch when the persisted mode already matches the target (track last-known mode; refresh via `GET /admin/mode` on poll). At most one switch per state change; a `409` (mode-switch restart in progress) is treated as a no-op and retried on a later tick.
- [ ] **Fail-closed everywhere:** endpoint failures, timeouts, network errors, and ambiguous responses yield no switch and never crash or block the plugin. On plugin restart the idle clock resets to "active now" (fail-safe: the proxy stays fast until a fresh full idle window passes).
- [ ] **Configurable via plugin settings** (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`): enabled toggle, idle threshold ms, poll interval ms; settings re-read every tick so changes apply without a plugin restart. The proxy URL is shared with the downtime worker (`downtimeProxyUrl`).
- [ ] **Coexistence with the proxy's built-in schedule:** the plugin's switches are manual overrides (the API's native semantics, LP-0MSMF25V9002AY1J); the proxy's time-based schedule (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00) reclaims control at its next boundary. Documented behavior, not a conflict.
- [ ] **Testing & validation:** unit tests cover idle-window evaluation, last-command tracking, cheap/fast switch triggers, restart reset, fail-closed paths, and settings clamps. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the herdr README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only **agent-route** commands count as operator activity (operator decision Q1).
- The cheap switch is gated on proxy idle — it must never kill in-flight work (operator decision Q4b).
- Mode switches never block the TUI or command dispatch: all HTTP calls are fire-and-forget (fast switch) or scheduled task work (cheap switch).
- Fail-closed at every boundary: no crash, no hammering, no repeated identical POSTs.
- The seed mentions "the `/admin/mode` API": `GET /admin/mode` only *reads* the mode; the switch endpoint is `POST /admin/set-mode`. The brief targets `/admin/set-mode`.

## Existing state

- Mode API + UI exist on the proxy: `GET /admin/mode`, `POST /admin/set-mode` (LP-0MSLMYEEU002IBH6); mode persisted in `proxy/.mode`, defaults to `fast`.
- Time-based automatic mode switching exists on the proxy (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00, LP-0MSM5K4TX004MICX) with manual-override persistence until the next scheduled change (LP-0MSMF25V9002AY1J). A mode switch restarts the proxy (terminates in-flight requests; clients retry — documented accepted behavior).
- The herdr plugin already has: settings system (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`, re-read per tick), a consolidated scheduler (worklist.ts), and a downtime worker that polls `/llama/local/status` with fail-closed idle evaluation (WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K + children). The mode-switch worker reuses this infrastructure.

## Desired change

Add a mode-switch worker to the herdr plugin:

1. `index.ts` `onCommand` (agent route) records `lastOperatorCommandAt = Date.now()` and fires the fast switch (`POST /admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}`, fire-and-forget, fail-open).
2. A new scheduler task (pattern-matched on the existing `downtime` task) ticks on `modeSwitchPollIntervalMs`: if `lastOperatorCommandAt` is null/older than the threshold AND the proxy is idle (reuse the local-status poller/idle evaluation), POST `/admin/set-mode {"mode":"cheap"}` — skipping when the persisted mode already is cheap.
3. New settings: `modeSwitchEnabled`, `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs`, `modeSwitchPollIntervalMs` (reusing `downtimeProxyUrl`); re-read each tick.
4. Restart behavior: worker construction sets `lastOperatorCommandAt = Date.now()` (reset to active).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` — new worker: idle-window evaluation, mode-state tracking, `/admin/set-mode` HTTP client (POST) + `GET /admin/mode` read, fail-closed
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` — unit tests (test-first)
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — new settings keys + clamps + defaults
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — scheduler task wiring + TUI options plumbing
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — agent-route hook: record last-command timestamp + fire fast switch
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — settings and behavior documentation

## Related work

- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime" (parent of the downtime worker; the poller/settings/scheduler infrastructure this feature reuses)
- **LP-0MSLMYEEU002IBH6** (llm-manager) — Web API/UI to toggle fast/cheap modes (the `/admin/mode` + `/admin/set-mode` endpoints)
- **LP-0MSM5K4TX004MICX** (llm-manager) — Time-based automatic mode switching (built-in schedule)
- **LP-0MSMF25V9002AY1J** (llm-manager) — API mode override persists until the next scheduled change
- **WL-0MSMIPPJI007GU9N / LP-0MSMZOAJW002UR2A** (llm-manager) — cheap-mode profile definition (2-slot pool)
- find-related automated report: WL-0MRCTZZ82000X7TM, WL-0MP15AMKV002F3U4, WL-0MS6AAW3M004JK9U (weak keyword matches; not design-relevant)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Mode switch restarts the proxy** (kills in-flight requests). Mitigated for the cheap direction by the idle gate (Q4b); the fast direction can still kill a cheap-mode downtime request when the operator returns — accepted (documented proxy behavior; the downtime dispatch's work retries on the next idle period).
- **Multiple plugin panes** could each run a mode-switch worker → duplicate POSTs. Same-mode POSTs are API noops and the worker skips already-matching modes, so the system converges; per-process single-flight is applied.
- **Schedule reassertion at boundaries** may flip the mode shortly after a plugin switch near a boundary — accepted; every new operator command re-switches to fast immediately (design intent).
- **`GET /admin/mode`/`POST /admin/set-mode` may not be reachable** from the plugin host — fail-closed (no switch), never crash; the plugin logs a warning.
- **Scope-creep risk:** related but out-of-scope opportunities (e.g., reflecting the active mode in the herdr UI, per-slot idle gating for the cheap switch, or activity-based mode tracking for non-plugin pi panes) are recorded as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** "operator-issued Pi command" ≡ agent-route commands routed through the herdr plugin (Q1). Commands issued directly in a pi pane (not via the plugin) are out of scope.
- **Assumption:** the existing idle evaluation (`evaluateIdle` with `requiredFreeSlots = 0`, all slots free) is the busy/idle gate for the cheap switch; if per-slot data later arrives (WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG), the gate follows the same semantics.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should only the agent-route commands (/skill:*, /intake, /plan, /prompt: → new pi pane) count as 'operator Pi commands' for the idle timer, or any command routed through the plugin?" — Answer (operator): "only agent-route". Source: interactive reply. Research: `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `routeCommand`/`isAgentCommand` distinguishes agent vs pane vs stdout routes.
- Q2: "Should the herdr plugin's activity-based switching (a) coexist as manual overrides — the schedule eventually reclaims control — or (b) fully own the mode while enabled?" — Answer (operator): clarified intent: "if the operator issues an agent-command it is *always* processed as 'fast', but if the operator leaves and the downtime dispatcher starts sending commands they are 'cheap'." Interpretation recorded: plugin switches are immediate manual overrides (fast on command, cheap on idle); the proxy's time schedule remains as a background fallback (coexistence, option a). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "After a plugin restart, should the idle clock (a) reset to 'active now' — stay fast until a fresh full idle window — or (b) treat restart as idle and switch to cheap immediately?" — Answer (operator): "a". Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Cheap-switch gating vs proxy busy state: (a) switch at the threshold unconditionally (can kill in-flight downtime dispatch), or (b) switch only when the proxy also reports idle?" — Answer (operator): "b". Source: interactive reply. Research: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `evaluateIdle`/`isIdleStatus`; `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/handlers.py` `/admin/set-mode` restart semantics.

- **WL-0MRCTZZ82000X7TM** – RCA: wl sync pre-push hook destroyed Tableau-Card-Engine repository (completed)

# Intake brief: Herdr — flipping `needsProducerReview` must not make a valid audit stale

**Work item:** WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R (bug, medium)

## Problem statement

Flipping the `needsProducerReview` flag (e.g. `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review true`, as the heartbeat does when flagging an item for producer review) bumps the work item's `updatedAt`. herdr's audit-freshness predicate `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` then reports the previously valid audit as **stale**, which (a) degrades the TUI audit icon from the passed glyph to the stale-passed/stage glyph, and (b) makes the downtime audit tier re-select the item for a wasteful `/skill:audit` re-run of unchanged content. A review-state flag is metadata, not content — it must not invalidate an audit.

## Users

- **Producer** — flips `needsProducerReview` (via TUI flag toggle or `wl update --needs-producer-review`) to signal review intent. Should see the item's existing green "audit passed" state unchanged.
  - User story: "As a producer, when I flag an item for review, I want its audit result to remain visibly passed, so I can trust that only genuinely changed items need re-auditing."
- **Herdr downtime worker** — dispatches `/skill:audit` for items without a valid audit during idle time. Should not burn an audit run on items whose only change since the audit was a review flag.
  - User story: "As the audit-tier dispatcher, I want to skip items whose audit is stale only because of a metadata flag flip, so idle time is spent auditing items whose content actually changed."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `WorklogDatabase.update()` persists a `needsProducerReview`-only change but **preserves** `updatedAt` (no bump). A change to any content field (title, description, status, stage, priority, sortIndex, parentId, tags, assignee, issueType, risk, effort) still bumps `updatedAt` exactly as today.
- [ ] Unit test (packages/shared): `update()` with only `needsProducerReview` flipped → flag persisted, `updatedAt` unchanged.
- [ ] Unit test (packages/shared): `update()` with a content field + flag in the same call → `updatedAt` bumped (combined update still bumps).
- [ ] Regression (packages/shared): no-op update and content-only update behave exactly as today (no-op preserves, content bumps).
- [ ] Herdr integration verification: after a flag-only update, `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` remains **true** for a previously fresh audit → TUI shows the passed icon (not the stale glyph) and `selectAuditCandidate` does **not** select the item (no redundant `/skill:audit` dispatch). Herdr code itself is unchanged (single source of truth stays in worklog).
- [ ] Documentation: comment on `update()`/the `fieldsToCompare` split documents why `needsProducerReview` is excluded from the timestamp-bump trigger; the `isAuditFresh` doc comment in `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` notes the guarantee ("flag-only flips do not move `updatedAt`").
- [ ] All related documentation updated (code comments, README/docs as applicable).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the **worklog core** (`packages/shared/src/database.ts` `update()`), per operator decision — not in herdr. herdr's `isAuditFresh` and `selectAuditCandidate` stay untouched; they automatically benefit once `updatedAt` stops moving on flag flips.
- Do not change the meaning of `updatedAt` for content changes: sync field-conflict resolution ("newer `updatedAt` wins", `src/sync.ts`) and `wl recent` ordering rely on it. Accepted caveat (operator-approved): a flag-only flip no longer bumps `updatedAt`, so a concurrent remote content edit could out-rank the flag in a field-conflict merge (low severity — the flag is a review signal, not content).
- The no-op fast path (`hasChanged` false → preserve `updatedAt`, no store write) must remain; the flag-only path must still **write** the flag while preserving the timestamp (it must not take the early return).
- `needsProducerReview` is the only field moved to the no-bump set; no other fields change semantics (minimal, surgical).
- Out of scope: the audit skill's own pipeline freshness (already handled by the content-fingerprint gate, SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT — a flag flip doesn't change the fingerprint); WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE (at-or-near freshness for the audit's own persistence write) is a separate item.

## Existing state

1. `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `update()`: `fieldsToCompare` includes `needsProducerReview`; if any tracked field changed → `updated.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()`.
2. `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)`: `auditTime > updateTime - 60000` (60 s buffer). A post-audit `updatedAt` bump → not fresh → stale.
3. `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` `getIconPrefix()` (line ~367): for `in_review`, `fresh ? auditIcon(...) : (auditResult === true ? auditStaleIcon(...) : stageIcon(...))` — the stale glyph path.
4. `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `selectAuditCandidate()` (line ~1043): filters `!isAuditFresh(c.auditedAt, c.updatedAt)` → stale item becomes an audit-dispatch candidate (subject to 7-day recency window and dispatched-marker exclusion).
5. `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `getNextAuditCandidate()` (line ~371): audit tier pulls candidates from `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` and routes through `selectAuditCandidate`.
6. Heartbeat (`skill/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py`) flags the next ready item via `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review true` — the trigger of the reported symptom.

## Desired change

In `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `update()`, split the change detection:

- `contentFieldsToCompare` = current `fieldsToCompare` **minus** `needsProducerReview` — any change here bumps `updatedAt` (unchanged behavior).
- `needsProducerReview` is a **metadata** field: a flag-only change persists the flag but preserves `updatedAt` (does not take the no-op early return, and does not bump the timestamp).
- Combined content+flag change → bump (as today).
- herdr: **no code change**; add/refresh a doc comment on `isAuditFresh` stating the guarantee and re-verify the icon + dispatch behavior via tests in `packages/herdr`.

## Key Files:

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `WorklogDatabase.update()`; split `fieldsToCompare` into content (bump) vs metadata (`needsProducerReview`, preserve `updatedAt`); keep the no-op fast path distinct from the flag-only path
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` (or existing shared test location) — new unit tests: flag-only (persist, preserve), content+flag (bump), no-op, content-only (unchanged behavior)
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — doc comment on `isAuditFresh` (guarantee: flag-only flips do not move `updatedAt`); no logic change
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — no change; referenced for verification that `selectAuditCandidate` stops selecting flag-staled items
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.test.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — integration-style regression checks (fresh audit after flag-only update → passed icon, not a dispatch candidate)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Sync conflict (accepted, low):** `src/sync.ts` field-conflict resolution picks the newer `updatedAt`; a flag-only flip no longer bumps it, so a concurrent remote content edit could out-rank the flag in a conflict merge. Mitigation: the flag is a review signal, not content — re-flagging is cheap and the next sync merge reconciles. Operator-approved in Q1.
- **`wl recent` ordering:** `src/commands/recent.ts` sorts by `updatedAt`; flag flips will no longer surface items as "recently updated". Arguably more correct (a review flag is not activity); document in the change notes.
- **Herdr dispatch recency window:** a flag-only flip no longer extends the 7-day audit-recency window (`DOWNTIME_AUDIT_RECENCY_WINDOW_MS`) — an old item flagged for review stays outside the window, unchanged from today (recency is about content activity, not review intent).
- **Scope-creep guard:** WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE (at-or-near freshness for the audit's own persistence write) is a separate item — do not fold it in here. The alternative "content-version signal" approach (Q1 option B) is explicitly out of scope.
- **Assumption:** herdr is the only timestamp-freshness consumer that matters for this bug; `heartbeat.py` checks `wl audit-show` rawOutput ("Ready to close: Yes"), not freshness, so it is unaffected either way.

## Related work

- WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE (open, bug, medium) — "Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher": *opposite direction* (audit's own persistence write must not look stale). Shares the same `isAuditFresh` predicate; complement, not duplicate. Coordinate so the two fixes don't conflict on the predicate.
- WL-0MS1OJZL7005CR7A (completed) — "Show distinct icon when audit is stale but readyToClose is true": introduced the stale-passed icon behavior.
- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG (completed) — "Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit": the audit-tier dispatch feature.
- WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (completed) — "Audit candidate selection".
- SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT (SorraAgents) — content-fingerprint freshness gate in the audit runner; the pipeline-side precedent for "non-content updates must not invalidate an audit".
- WL-0MLGTWT4S1X4HDD9 / WL-0MLQ0ZHQE0JBX8Y6 (completed) — `--needs-producer-review` filter and TUI shortcut; the flag feature this fix interacts with.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should the fix live? (A) Worklog core — `wl update` persists a `needsProducerReview`-only change but preserves `updatedAt` (flag is metadata, not content), fixing herdr display + dispatch with one change; caveat: sync field-conflict resolution could drop a flag flip racing a concurrent remote content edit. (B) Herdr-side only — requires worklog to emit a new content-version signal (bigger). (C) Both / other." — Answer (user): **A — Worklog core**. Source: interactive reply. # Intake Draft: Downtime dispatcher — priority-first selection with round-robin tie-break across tied items + jittered probes

## Problem statement

When multiple instances of the herdr plugin are active on the same machine, the same instance often wins the race to dispatch in downtime — with a deterministic ascending-sortIndex tie-break, the same lowest-sortIndex item is always picked first by whichever instance is fastest, so one instance monopolises dispatch and tied-priority items are never rotated. Probes also fire in lockstep (all instances at the same fixed poll interval), which amplifies the same-winner effect and gives other machines no chance to get into the loop.

## Users

- **Operator with several herdr panes/instances on one machine** — wants the downtime work spread fairly: highest-priority items first, tied-priority items rotated round-robin, and no single instance hogs all dispatches.
- **Operator with multiple machines sharing the llama proxy** — wants probes desynchronised so each machine gets a fair chance to dispatch first.

### User stories

- As an operator running N herdr instances on one machine, when multiple candidates tie on priority, I want them dispatched in round-robin rotation (shared across instances) so no single item/instance dominates.
- As an operator with several machines on the proxy, I want each downtime probe delayed by a random amount (within ±50% of the poll interval) so instances do not probe in lockstep and other machines can win the dispatch race.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Priority-first selection is preserved: a higher-priority candidate is always selected before any lower-priority candidate, regardless of round-robin state (all tiers: audit, implement, plan/intake).
- [ ] Round-robin tie-break: among candidates sharing the same priority level, selection rotates through them using a shared, durable cursor persisted under `<cwd>/.worklog/` (e.g. `downtime-round-robin.json`), so repeated dispatches of a tied group do not always pick the same item; two instances selecting from the same group pick different items when the cursor has advanced. Unit tests cover rotation across repeated selections and across the three tier selectors.
- [ ] Shared state is fail-open and never blocks dispatch: a missing, unreadable, or corrupt round-robin file degrades to default (no rotation) behaviour; the cursor write failure is tolerated (marker/log write ordering unchanged — the dispatched-marker remains the authoritative guard against re-dispatch).
- [ ] Probe jitter: the downtime task's effective poll interval is jittered ±50% of the configured `downtimePollIntervalMs` per tick (random, injectable RNG for deterministic tests); two workers with identical configuration do not probe in lockstep. Jitter range is verified by unit tests (min/max bounds).
- [ ] Absorbs WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6 (Stagger herdr plugin downtime checks) — the jitter subsumes the stagger intent; that item is marked absorbed/blocked-by this item.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Round-robin grouping key is the **priority level** (critical/high/medium/low), not sortIndex (operator answer).
- Coordination state lives in the existing shared `.worklog/` files — no new daemons, no DB schema change.
- Jitter range is exactly ±50% of the configured poll interval (operator answer).
- Fail-closed / fail-open conventions preserved at every boundary (existing design doctrine); round-robin must never weaken the existing dispatched-marker exclusion or the CAS claim.
- No scope creep: no changes to `wl` CLI selection order (`src/commands`), the Pi TUI mirror, or the grouping/fetcher list ordering.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) runs tiers in order: audit → implement → plan (`intake_complete`) → intake (`idea`).
- Selection (`selectNextCandidate` / `selectAuditCandidate` / `selectImplementCandidate`) sorts candidates ascending by `sortIndex` and picks the first — deterministic, so a tied group always resolves to the same item; the fastest instance wins the CAS claim every time.
- Scheduler (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) registers a fixed-interval `downtime` task (`intervalMs = downtimePollIntervalMs`, default 30s); all instances poll in lockstep.
- Dispatch markers (`downtime-dispatches.log`) + CAS claim (WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN) prevent double-dispatch of the same item but do not address "same instance always wins" or tied-item rotation.

## Desired change

1. **Shared round-robin registry** (`<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-round-robin.json`): map priority level → last-dispatched item id (or rotation cursor). New read/write helpers alongside `downtime-log.ts` (same fail-open discipline). Selection consults the registry: among same-priority candidates, pick the item after the cursor; record the pick before dispatch (write-then-spawn ordering, mirroring the dispatched-marker discipline).
2. **Jittered probes**: the downtime scheduler task's effective interval = `downtimePollIntervalMs + uniform(-50%..+50%)` per tick (injectable RNG; deterministic tests). This absorbs the stagger intent of WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — round-robin selection logic (`selectNextCandidate`, `selectAuditCandidate`, `selectImplementCandidate` gain a rotation-aware variant or shared helper); jitter helper.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — new `downtime-round-robin.json` read/write helpers (mirror existing dispatch-log helpers).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — downtime scheduler task uses jittered interval per tick.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire rotation registry path into `createDowntimeDeps`/`createDowntimeWorker` (cwd-scoped).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — only if the interval-mutation approach needs a small hook (prefer mutating the task's `intervalMs` inside its run, which the scheduler already re-reads at reschedule time).
- Tests: `downtime-worker.test.ts`, `downtime-log.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts` / `scheduler.test.ts`.

## Related work

- WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6 — Stagger herdr plugin downtime checks (open, medium): **absorbed by this item** (probe jitter supersedes).
- WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN — Downtime dispatcher: conditional claim + marker exclusion (completed): the CAS/claim infra this builds on; round-robin must compose with it.
- WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (completed): context for the marker/CAS design points.
- WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — Log herdr downtime dispatches (completed): the `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` pattern reused for the round-robin file.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** round-robin rotates *items within a priority level* and is shared across instances on one machine via the local `.worklog/` file; cross-machine fairness relies on jitter + the existing CAS claim (no cross-machine shared state) — consistent with operator answers.
- **Risk:** cursor-write races between instances on the same file. Mitigation: reuse the existing flock/atomic-rename pattern used by the dispatch log; a lost update degrades to a repeated pick, never a wrong-priority pick.
- **Risk:** jitter delays dispatch by up to +50% of the poll interval when a machine would otherwise be first. Accepted per operator instruction (fairness over latency).
- **Risk (scope creep):** do not extend round-robin into `wl` CLI ordering or list rendering; tie-break is a herdr-client concern. Extra opportunities (e.g. cross-machine leases) are recorded as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Round-robin scope — across instances (competing herdr instances take turns) or across items (tied-priority items dispatched in rotation)?" — Answer (user): "(b) across items — when several items tie on priority, they get dispatched in rotation." Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-14.
- Q2: "Coordination mechanism — shared state in `.worklog/` or purely instance-local probabilistic?" — Answer (user): "existing is fine" (shared `.worklog/` files acceptable). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Random delay bounds — range and placement (between probes only, or also pre-dispatch backoff)?" — Answer (user): "±50% of the poll interval" (between probes). Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Tie definition — same priority level regardless of sortIndex, or identical sortIndex?" — Answer (user): "(a) same priority level (critical/high/medium/low)". Source: interactive reply.
- Q5: "Rotation state scope — shared (one rotation per priority group in `.worklog/`) or per-instance?" — Answer (user): "(a) shared — all instances on the machine rotate together". Source: interactive reply.
- Q6: "Relationship to existing stagger item WL-0MSMHX6IR007F3H6?" — Answer (user): "absorb". Source: interactive reply.

# Exclude child items from audit-tier dispatch selection

## Problem statement

The audit-tier dispatch selects items from `completed` / `in_review` work items without a valid audit, but currently includes child items (sub-tasks) alongside parent items. Child items should never be dispatched independently — only parent items should appear in the audit dispatch tier.

## Users

- **Producers reviewing epics** — the completed/in_review review queue should contain parent items only, so the audit dispatch focuses on reviewing actual deliverable units, not sub-tasks.
- **Downtime dispatcher** — when dispatching `/skill:audit` during idle time, it should only spawn audits for parent items, never for children.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` uses `--root-only` on the `wl list` call so that only items without a parent are returned as audit candidates.
2. All existing audit-tier tests pass with the change (candidates should be unaffected unless they are children, which should now be excluded).
3. If a test or scenario creates child items in `completed`/`in_review`, those children are never returned as audit candidates.
4. Documentation updated: code comments in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` reflecting the root-only constraint; README downtime section updated.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- This is a minimal surgical change: only the `wl list` arguments in `getNextAuditCandidate` need modification (add `--root-only`).
- No changes to the implement-tier selection are in scope — that tier uses `wl next`, which already respects parent-child hierarchy (per completed items WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1 and WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR).

## Existing state

- `getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` calls:
  ```
  wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json
  ```
- `wl list` supports a `--root-only` flag that shows only items without a parent.
- Parent-child hierarchy was already addressed in `wl list` (WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR) and `wl next` (WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1, WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1).

## Desired change

Add `--root-only` to the `wl list` call in `getNextAuditCandidate`:
```
wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json
```

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getNextAuditCandidate` function (line ~405): add `--root-only` to `buildWlArgs` call.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — interface doc comment for `getNextAuditCandidate` may need updating to reflect root-only contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — audit selection tests may need a test confirming children are excluded.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — downtime section (update if documenting selection rules).

## Related work

- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** — Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr) — introduces `--root-only` flag on `wl list`.
- **WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1** — wl next should return parent items instead of surfacing children individually — ensures `wl next` returns parents, not children.
- **WL-0MSI9WPNI0044RL8** — Audit dispatch tier — establishes the audit tier concept.
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** — Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit — audit tier wiring.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY** — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions — parent for audit-tier dispatched-marker exclusion.
- **WL-0MSLUASNF001LLAT** — Dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection — child of above.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** If existing tests create child items in `completed`/`in_review`, they were previously valid candidates and now will be excluded — test fixtures may need updating to use root items.
- **Risk:** If ALL `completed`/`in_review` items happen to be children (extremely rare), the audit tier returns no candidates — this is the correct behavior (no root items to audit).
- **Assumption:** `--root-only` does not change the JSON output shape — verified against `wl list --help` (it is a filter flag, not a format modifier).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Implement-tier selection (`wl next`) already respects parent-child hierarchy (per WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1); no changes needed there. If implement-tier also needs explicit `--root-only`, that is a separate work item.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Does this apply to the implement tier as well?" — Answer (operator): Only the audit tier is in scope. The implement tier (`wl next`) already returns parent items instead of children (WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1). — Source: interactive reply.

# Intake Brief: Dispatching continues while downtime dispatch is disabled

**Work item:** WL-0MT4BWUHW008LIFE · **Type:** bug · **Priority:** critical (operator-specified)
**Date:** 2026-08-22

## Problem statement

The operator disables downtime dispatch via the `d` shortcut (header shows
`[Downtime Off]` on the pane) yet pi agent work continues to be dispatched —
audits, plans and implementations keep spawning, and the ContextHub audit
`WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU` was dispatched at 11:05:23Z while the operator believed
dispatch was disabled. The same herdr worklist header later reported
`[⏳ downtime idle 40+ min]` — the enabled-and-idle worker state — in a
session the operator considers disabled. The disable control is not
effective, not durable, or not scoped the way the operator believes.

## Users

- **Herdr operators (multi-workspace)**: disable downtime dispatch to stop
  autonomous work (e.g. while working interactively), and expect that disable
  to hold — without needing to also stop every sibling pane or remember
  in-memory semantics.
  - As an operator I press `d`, see `[Downtime Off]`, and **no** new pi agent
    panes spawn anywhere for that worklog root until I re-enable dispatch.
  - As an operator I can tell, at a glance, which pane(s) are disabled and
    which are still dispatching.

## Acceptance Criteria (initial; refine at plan)

1. **Disabled ⇒ no dispatch, durably.** After one `d` press (header shows
   `[Downtime Off]`), with no further key presses and no manual settings edit,
   the worklist's downtime worker performs no proxy polling, no idle
   tracking, and no dispatch **for at least 60 minutes** (i.e. well past the
   4-minute idle threshold and any 60-minute no-candidate cooldown window).
   Verified by a test that toggles the worker off, advances simulated time
   through the threshold/cooldown boundaries, and asserts zero
   `dispatchDowntimeWork` invocations and zero pane spawns.
2. **No silent re-enable.** If the per-instance override can be lost by any
   real pane/plugin lifecycle event (restart, reload, re-attach), the
   operator must be told explicitly (header/status must not silently return
   to `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` in a pane previously shown `[Downtime Off]`).
   The chosen fix must make the disable state either (a) durable across those
   events, or (b) visibly non-durable with an explicit notice — never a
   silent revert.
3. **Toggle cycle cannot force-enable.** Pressing `d` twice must never leave
   dispatch force-enabled (`override === true`) while the operator believes
   they disabled it: the second press returns to "follow settings" (`null`),
   or re-enable requires explicit confirmation. A test pins the full cycle
   `null → false → null` (or `null → false → (confirmed) true` — decided at
   plan) and asserts `enabled` after each step.
4. **Header honesty.** `renderDowntimeStatus` must never render
   `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` (an enabled, polling worker) in a pane whose
   dispatch gate the operator disabled: the rendered state must always agree
   with the effective dispatch decision of `tick()`. Test: render off /
   enabled / paused / dispatching states against the worker's effective
   enabled state.
5. **Per-pane scope is visible & documented.** The per-instance scope of the
   `d` toggle is preserved (sibling panes unaffected), but the README/help
   makes the scope explicit ("current pane only, in-memory, resets on
   restart"), and each pane's header state (`[Downtime Off]` vs live status)
   lets the operator tell which pane is disabled. Docs updated; acceptance: a
   user reading the README cannot reasonably believe `d` disables dispatch
   for all panes or persists across restarts.
6. **Root-cause regression evidence.** The reproducing evidence for the
   reported incident — ContextHub audit `WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU` dispatched
   2026-08-22T11:05:23Z while dispatch was believed disabled, and the
   subsequent 11:05–11:47Z multi-root dispatch wave — is explained by the
   confirmed root cause in a comment/AC write-up, with the confirmation
   steps used (dispatch-log, herdr pane-spawn log, header state).
7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (including the
   existing downtime-worker / toggle test suites
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`).

## Constraints

- The per-instance in-memory toggle design (WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF AC2) may be
  changed ONLY where needed to satisfy AC2/AC3; settings file writes and
  cross-pane coupling need explicit operator sign-off at plan.
- Existing dispatch guarantees must not regress: code-freeze gate, dispatched
  marker exclusion, per-tier free-slot minimums, single-flight, no-candidate
  cooldown (see RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT and
  `packages/herdr/docs/downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`).
- No new dispatch side channels: the fix must not add or remove a dispatch
  mechanism; it only changes when the existing worker dispatches.

## Existing state

- The `d` shortcut (shortcuts.json) → `/downtime toggle` →
  `onDowntimeToggle()` → `downtimeWorker.toggle()` (index.ts:1000-1046,
  worklist.ts:3346-3352).
- `toggle()` cycles the in-memory override `null → false → true → null`
  (downtime-worker.ts:1639-1641): **a second press force-enables dispatch
  (override = true)**, which also overrides a settings-level disable.
- `tick()` short-circuits when `!(override ?? cfg.enabled)`
  (downtime-worker.ts:1658-1661) — the gate is correct for a single worker
  instance.
- `renderDowntimeStatus` (worklist.ts:2771-2799) renders either
  `[Downtime Off]` (disabled) or `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`
  (enabled + polling): mutually exclusive for one pane.
- The toggle is **in-memory and per-instance**: plugin/pane restart resets
  `override` to `null` (follows settings) with no notice; sibling panes are
  unaffected. Leader-only dispatch (WL-0MSXHA1B0005G3E5) is blocked, so
  multiple panes dispatch concurrently.
- Observed evidence 2026-08-22 (report incident):
  - ContextHub `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`: audit
    `WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU` dispatched 11:05:23Z (cwd ContextHub); last entry
    for this root.
  - herdr-server.log: four dispatch panes spawned simultaneously 11:05:09–
    11:05:23Z across SorraAgents / open_source_llm / Tableau-Card-Engine /
    ContextHub (pids 302077/302156/302252/302464); further panes 11:12Z,
    11:15Z, 11:42Z, 11:47Z (sibling roots only).
  - No worklist-pane (plugin) restart is evident in herdr-server.log between
    the incident and the report; the `/downtime toggle` press itself is not
    recorded in worklog-command-log.json (internal action, unlogged).
  - Config `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` has no `downtimeEnabled`
    key → all workers enabled by default.

## Desired change

Downtime dispatch, once disabled, must actually stop dispatching for the
worklog root the operator is controlling and stay stopped until explicitly
re-enabled — with the header state always agreeing with the effective gate,
and with the per-pane/in-memory scope either made durable or made explicit.
Root-cause confirmation at implementation must decide between (ranked):

- **H1 — override lost/cycled after the press:** pane/plugin lifecycle or a
  second `d` press reverted the override (`null` → settings-enabled, or
  `false` → `true` force-on). Explains the audit dispatch at 11:05:23Z and
  the later idle-40+min header. Validation: reproduce toggle → restart /
  second press → assert dispatch resumes silently (AC2/AC3).
- **H2 — in-flight dispatch completed after the press:** a dispatch already
  running when `d` was pressed completed (single-flight; marker written after
  spawn). Explains one late dispatch, not the continued idle reporting.
  Validation: press `d` while `dispatching === true`; assert the in-flight
  dispatch still logs (acceptable) but no NEW dispatch starts (AC1).
- **H3 — scope mismatch:** the observed dispatch came from another enabled
  pane (sibling workspace/root) while the toggled pane was correctly off.
  Explains continuing sibling-root dispatches and an idle header in an
  untoggled pane. Validation: enumerate panes/workspaces, reproduce
  per-instance toggle (AC5).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `toggle()` cycle (~1639),
  `tick()` gate (~1658), `createDowntimeWorker` override lifecycle; where
  durable-override and cycle fixes land.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `renderDowntimeStatus` (~2771),
  `/downtime toggle` routing (3346), scheduler task registration (5066);
  header-honesty fix, persisted-state notice, README-adjacent help hints.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — worker wiring + `onDowntimeToggle`
  (~1000-1046); sole `createDowntimeWorker` call site.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `PluginSettings` schema (43-79);
  durable override key if persistence is chosen (constraint: needs sign-off).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `d` → `/downtime toggle` (line 4).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — scope/durability documentation (AC5).
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`.
- Evidence: `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`,
  `~/.config/herdr/herdr-server.log`,
  `~/.config/herdr/worklog-command-log.json`.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF** — Shortcut key to toggle downtime dispatch per
  herdr instance (parent design; in_review). AC2 mandates in-memory
  per-instance; AC4 mandates the tick short-circuit. This bug is the first
  real-world failure of that design's durability/scope expectations.
- **WL-0MSZS1NNV0075NFI** — Header rendering `[Downtime Off]` (completed).
- **WL-0MSZS1OHV0067JD1** — README docs for `d` / `[Downtime Off]`
  (completed; docs now need the scope/durability caveat).
- **WL-0MSXHA1B0005G3E5** — Leader-only dispatch logic (blocked): while
  unimplemented, multiple panes dispatch concurrently, amplifying any
  per-pane disable gap.
- **WL-0MT47BMR7003ZQ66** — Active-audit single-flight tests (open): audit
  dispatch multiplicity guard, adjacent to the reported multi-dispatch wave.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY / WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** — Prior downtime dispatch
  duplication RCA + fix (completed): dispatch-path guarantees this fix must
  not regress.
- Docs: `packages/herdr/docs/downtime-config-audit-2026-08-08.md`,
  `packages/herdr/docs/downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — single root cause may not exist:** the evidence is
  consistent with H1+H3 jointly (override lost AND sibling panes dispatching
  regardless). ACs are written against the observable contract so the fix
  covers the failure class, not one mechanism.
- **Risk — persistence changes settings semantics:** making the override
  durable (e.g. writing a per-project marker) touches the shared settings /
  marker files and could affect multi-pane behavior; needs operator sign-off
  at plan (constraint).
- **Risk — scope creep:** attractive extras (global kill switch, per-project
  master disable, leader-only completion) are adjacent but out of scope;
  file as follow-ups, do not fold in.
- **Mitigation — evidence kit preserved:** dispatch log, herdr pane-spawn
  log excerpts and header-state observations are recorded above and in work
  item comments so the implementer can verify the confirmed root cause
  without guessing.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How did you disable dispatching? (a) pressed `d` → header showed
  `[Downtime Off]` on the pane you were looking at; (b) set `downtimeEnabled:
  false` in the herdr config; (c) something else?" — Answer (operator,
  interactive): **(a)** pressed `d`, header showed `[Downtime Off]`.
- Q2: "Where does the 'idle 40+ minutes' report appear?" — Answer
  (operator, interactive): **the herdr worklist header
  (`[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`)**.
- Q3: "Which audit dispatch violated your disable intent?" — Answer
  (operator, interactive): **`WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU`** (ContextHub root;
  dispatched 2026-08-22T11:05:23Z per dispatch log; pane spawned
  11:05:23.495Z per herdr-server.log).
- OPEN QUESTION 1: Was `d` pressed exactly once in the flagged pane, or more
  than once? (Discriminates H1-cycle from H1-restart / H3.)
- OPEN QUESTION 2: Which workspace/tab displayed `[Downtime Off]` vs the
  header showing `[⏳ downtime idle 40+ min]` — the same pane or different
  panes? (Discriminates H3.)
- OPEN QUESTION 3: Was the flagged worklist pane restarted/re-attached
  between the `d` press and the observed dispatch? (herdr-server.log shows no
  plugin-pane respawn in the window, but herdr may not log all lifecycle
  events.)
## Related work (automated report)
